memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Recurrent itchy wheals for three months.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: The patient reports daily episodes of raised, erythematous wheals with intense itching, lasting less than 24 hours, no identifiable trigger.
EXAMINATION: Vital signs: BP 122/78 mmHg, pulse 78/min. Weight 68 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 23.5 (overweight). Skin shows scattered wheals on trunk and limbs, no angioedema. No mucosal lesions.
IMPRESSION: Chronic idiopathic urticaria. No signs of systemic disease.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start levocetirizine 5 mg orally once daily. Advise non‑sedating antihistamine as needed, keep a symptom diary, avoid known allergens, wear loose clothing. Since BMI ≥23, counsel balanced diet and regular aerobic activity 150 min/week. Offered influenza vaccine; patient declined. Return if wheals become painful, develop angioedema, difficulty swallowing, fever >39°C, or widespread rash.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Allergy to dust mites: sneezing, nasal congestion, itchy eyes on exposure.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Persistent urticaria despite antihistamine.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports continued daily wheals, slightly less intense, still requiring antihistamine most days.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/76 mmHg, weight 66 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 22.8. Skin shows fewer wheals, mild excoriations from scratching.
IMPRESSION: Chronic urticaria with mild eosinophilia on CBC; TSH normal. Symptom control partial.
ARRANGEMENTS: Stop levocetirizine; start cetirizine 10 mg at bedtime. Continue symptom diary, avoid triggers, maintain regular activity. Offered influenza vaccine; patient accepted, vaccine administered today. Return if wheals increase, angioedema, fever >39°C, or signs of infection.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: WBC 6.2 x10^9/L (4-10), Neutrophils 4.0, Lymphocytes 1.5, Eosinophils 0.6 (0.0-0.5) slightly elevated. Hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL (13-17). Platelets 250 x10^9/L (150-400).
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L (0.4-4.0). Free T4: 12.5 pmol/L (9-19).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Urticaria flare after work stress.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports increased wheals over past two weeks, linked to stressful periods at the flower shop, with mild facial swelling.
EXAMINATION: BP 120/78 mmHg, weight 67 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 23.2 (overweight). Skin shows scattered wheals on arms and neck, no angioedema.
IMPRESSION: Chronic urticaria exacerbated by psychological stress; labs previously normal.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue cetirizine 10 mg HS, add levocetirizine 5 mg OD for breakthrough symptoms. Advise stress‑reduction techniques, regular exercise, and maintain BMI‑appropriate diet. Offered influenza vaccine; patient already vaccinated. Return if wheals become painful, angioedema, difficulty breathing, fever >39°C, or widespread rash.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling more stressed at work lately, and the hives have gotten worse, especially on my forearms after a busy day.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2026-02-05 at 10:00 AM with Dr Priya Natarajan.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Urticaria improved on combined antihistamines.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports fewer wheals, only occasional mild itching, no angioedema in the past month.
EXAMINATION: BP 119/76 mmHg, weight 66 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 22.8. Skin shows faint scattered wheals, no active lesions.
IMPRESSION: Chronic urticaria, well controlled on cetirizine HS and levocetirizine OD. No laboratory abnormalities noted previously.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue cetirizine 10 mg HS and levocetirizine 5 mg OD. Advise to continue stress‑management, regular activity, and maintain weight. Offered influenza vaccine for next season; patient to receive in autumn. Return if wheals increase, angioedema, fever >39°C, or signs of infection.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Skin prick test performed with common aeroallergens (dust mite, pollen, mold). Results: mild reactivity to dust mite (2+ wheal), negative for pollen and mold.
